content:
nisha: bringing up community LlamaX-13B q4_8bit on dedicated staging, seeing early termination in streaming. model returns short responses and then stops with a phantom eos. anyone seen multi-eos / special-token shenanigans before?

liam: can you paste a raw stream log or stdout? curious if it's an actual eos id or our stop-seq matching in the frontend. :eyes: 

nisha: pasted below, small repro. note the generated token ids and the decoded text. streaming chunks show an <eos> sent from runtime, then again a decoded "" on next chunk which kills the stream.

nisha: ```
[stream] chunk 1: ids=[50256, 187, 45] text="Hello, the model says"
[stream] chunk 2: ids=[50256] text=""  <-- runtime emitted eos id 50256 here
[stream] chunk 3: ids=[50256, 11] text=""
```

maria: 50256 is the HF sentinel for '' right? seems like tokenizer has it as both eos and as an additional_special_token in this repo's tokenizer.json. that double-mapping can cause decoding to emit it twice depending on merge rules.

omkar: also check model config.json from HF -> maybe `eos_token_id` is set but `additional_special_tokens` includes the same string. show config.json please.

nisha: config snippet from the packaged repo: ```json
{"eos_token_id":50256, "bos_token_id":1, "additional_special_tokens":["",""], "chat_template":"<|system|>{system}\n<|user|>{user}\n<|assistant|>"}
```

liam: aha — duplicate entries in additional_special_tokens. HF tokenizers sometimes keep an internal mapping where a special token can be both an EOS and an extra token. When tokenization merges subtokens across chunk boundaries streaming can produce the sentinel twice.

maria: also our chat template injects role markers that end up being tokenized to a trailing eos-like sentinel in some merges. combo of chat template + duplicate special token = early stop.

nisha: repro notes: when I encode the prompt with HF tokenizer locally, I get a single 50256 at the end. But when we run the runtime's merge/token-join path on quantized weights (GGML style) the generator emits 50256, then due to subtoken boundary buffering it emits it again as a separate token. The serving runtime then treats ANY eos_token_id emission as terminal and closes the stream immediately.

omkar: proposed fixes: (1) dedupe additional_special_tokens in tokenizer.json and ensure eos_token is not repeated, (2) runtime: change streaming rule to treat consecutive identical eos_token_id emissions as a single event within a short window, (3) at API layer: prefer stop-sequences string matching instead of raw eos_id if client requested stop sequences.

liam: ^ agree. small runtime patch is low-risk: ignore eos if previous emitted id was same and time delta < 200ms or token count delta==0. That covers kernel re-emit races. But still we should fix tokenizer config upstream.

maria: for bringup checklist I recommend: include `tokenizer.save_pretrained()` artifacts from HF, assert `set(additional_special_tokens)` length equals list length (no dupes), verify `eos_token` string equals only one index, and run a quick streaming smoke test with different chunk sizes (1,4,8) to catch merge races.

nisha: quick patch I tried: removed the duplicate special token and re-uploaded model bundle. smoke tests passed locally. staging runtime still had one edge case where a quantized kernel emitted an extra 50256 when `max_new_tokens=1`. looks like an off-by-one in the kernel's finalize step. opened infra issue.

infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-789: "quant kernel finalize emits duplicate eos on single-token generations" — assigned to omkar. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-789

omkar: I'll look into kernel finalize. For now I'll land a runtime guard to coalesce consecutive identical eos emissions (small PR incoming). Also adding an E2E test in eng-ml that simulates token re-emit.

liam: thanks — can we also add a diagnostic endpoint that returns tokenizer mappings (eos_token_id, special_tokens list) for any model bundle id so we can spot config mismatches during onboarding?

maria: good call. I've got a small script that checks: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('path'); print(t.eos_token_id, t.all_special_tokens)"` — would be handy to run automatically in our conversion pipeline.

nisha: thanks team. summary: root cause = duplicate special token + kernel finalize re-emit. short-term: runtime coalesce + dedupe tokenizer configs on bundle. long-term: add conversion pipeline assertion + streaming e2e tests. I'll update the onboarding playbook. :+1: 

liam: ping me when PR is up, I'll review the runtime guard and the e2e test.

maria: adding a note to model catalog entry for LlamaX-13B-8bit to mark it as "required config patch applied" so we don't re-ingest bad bundle accidentally.

nisha: FYI if anyone needs the failing artifact I uploaded it to s3: s3://redwood-staging/artifacts/llamax-13b-q4-172850 . contains logs and the exact tokenizer.json used.

omkar: grabbing it now. will attach kernel debug logs to INFRA-789.

nisha: cheers — will follow up once runtime PR lands.

maria: :shipit:
